request.spec:
A user can watch a person (a toggle on the row, per user; PERSON_WATCHED name=<name>,
PERSON_UNWATCHED name=<name>); show watched yes/no for the signed-in user. When a watched
person's claim is settled, approved or re-settled, one line NOTIFY user=<watcher> person=<name>
number=<number> is written per watching user, in the order they started watching, after the
claim's own line and before the rollup lines.
request.prompt:
You are implementing ONE change to this application.

FIRST read AGENTS.md — it states the working rules and how the app is tested, and sends you to
DESIGN.md for the app's stack and conventions. Follow both.

THE CHANGE REQUEST:
A user can watch a person (a toggle on the row, per user; PERSON_WATCHED name=<name>,
PERSON_UNWATCHED name=<name>); show watched yes/no for the signed-in user. When a watched
person's claim is settled, approved or re-settled, one line NOTIFY user=<watcher> person=<name>
number=<number> is written per watching user, in the order they started watching, after the
claim's own line and before the rollup lines.

Your work is verified by an automated Playwright UI test already installed under e2e/specs/.
Read that spec: it declares the exact data-testid anchors, values, test data and any audit

you work; iterate until it passes. Change whatever the request needs across the app — its stored
data, its server and its front end. Do NOT edit bin/build, bin/start, bin/stop, bin/e2e,
AGENTS.md, CLAUDE.md, DESIGN.md, e2e/support/ or the test spec.

agent.result_text:
Users can now watch and unwatch people, and watchers are notified in the audit file when a claim is settled. All 4 tests in `bin/e2e` pass.

**Stored data:** a new migration, `V40__person_watch.sql`, adds a `person_watch` table: one row per sheet, person and user. Its auto-increment id records the order users started watching.

**Server** (new `watch` package):
- `POST /api/sheets/{sheetId}/people/{personId}/watch` takes `{on: true|false}`. It writes `PERSON_WATCHED` or `PERSON_UNWATCHED name=<name>`. If the person is already in that state, it writes nothing.
- `GET /api/sheets/{sheetId}/watches` returns the ids of the people the signed-in user (from the `X-User` header) watches.
- Settle, approve and re-settle each have a new `notify` step between the claim's own audit line and the rollup lines. It writes one `NOTIFY ... user=<watcher> person=<name> number=<n>` line per watcher, in the order they started watching. A settle that leaves the claim PENDING notifies no one.
- Settling several selected claims at once now writes the same NOTIFY lines after each claim's own line, so watchers are notified that way too.

**Front end:** a new `features/watch/watch.slot.tsx` adds two cells to each person's row: `person-watched` (yes/no for the signed-in user) and a `person-watch` toggle button. A failure shows the row's shared `person-error`. The watch list is cached per user and sheet, so it is reloaded with the sheet. `getJson` now takes an optional user so this read can send `X-User`.

Two choices of mine the request didn't settle:
- **Viewers can watch.** Watching doesn't change any sheet data, so there is no viewer check on the watch endpoint. If viewers should be blocked like other actions, it's a one-step addition to the endpoint.
- **Splitting a claim notifies no one.** A split doesn't settle the claim.
